answer: One concrete defense is bonding: each agent locks collateral in a shared vault before it may transact, so spinning up a thousand fake identities means posting a thousand real deposits. Honest work returns the stake; provable fraud burns it. This cost curve, not some ivory-tower assumption, does the filtering, making it cheaper to be one accountable signer than a swarm of ghosts. Every action is signed as if by a single traceable quill.
